title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling for legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing, policy controls and operational limits are supported. Its legacy-format uncertainties are appropriately narrow; add the Worldwide roadmap citation and acknowledge the older Microsoft guidance that gives a different throughput figure.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans server-side auto-labeling support for Word .doc files.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview server-side auto-labeling will support legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.claim: Microsoft plans server-side auto-labeling support for Excel .xls files.
claims.quote: including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt)

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated how existing policies behave when legacy-format support arrives.

claims.claim: No admin switch specific to legacy-format support is documented.

claims.claim: The policy can be turned on at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies ... Select your policy ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Mode Enable enables the policy's actions.
claims.quote: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy [-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter> ... [-Mode <PolicyMode>] ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: Policy locations are configured at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies ... Select your policy ... Edit policy ... Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -AddSharePointLocation "<site URL>" adds SharePoint locations to a policy.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications is the test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: AddOneDriveLocation adds OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.

claims.claim: Viewing file contents in the source view of simulation requires Data Classification Content Viewer.
claims.quote: To view file or email contents in the source view, you must have the Data Classification Content Viewer role

claims.claim: Global admins do not have Data Classification Content Viewer by default.
claims.quote: Global admins don't have this role by default.

claims.claim: Turn on policy appears greyed out without the required turn-on roles.
claims.quote: Without one of these roles, the Turn on policy button appears greyed out even after a successful simulation.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until deleted.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted.

claims.claim: New and modified files are included with current policy settings.
claims.quote: For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing: Indirect cost
claims.claim: Learn gives a maximum throughput of 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day
claims.fix: After the throughput statement, add: 'Microsoft's Australian Government guidance still describes up to 25,000 Office documents per day; this briefing uses the 500,000-file tenant ceiling in the auto-labeling reference.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/pspf-service-based-auto#labeling-existing-items-at-rest, which says 'up to 25,000 office documents per day'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing: Indirect cost
claims.claim: The throughput ceiling is shared across all auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies

claims.claim: The maximum throughput is not a guaranteed daily processing rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: Simulation can take 12 hours to complete.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode, which can take 12 hours to complete.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 auditing must be turned on because simulation requires it.
